name: Third-Party Integration
description: Third-Party Integration standard. Defines enforceable rules, implementation boundaries, failure handling and review evidence expected when STD-INTEGRATION applies.

rules.title: Wrap third-party services behind an owned boundary
rules.detail: Application/domain code should depend on an internal interface/model so vendor-specific details remain localized.
rules.example_good: The implementation and review evidence demonstrate: Wrap third-party services behind an owned boundary.
rules.example_bad: The change violates or ignores the rule: Wrap third-party services behind an owned boundary.

rules.title: Define timeout, retry, rate-limit and failure behavior
rules.detail: Every remote integration specifies bounded timeout, retryable conditions, backoff, quotas and degraded behavior.
rules.example_good: The implementation and review evidence demonstrate: Define timeout, retry, rate-limit and failure behavior.
rules.example_bad: The change violates or ignores the rule: Define timeout, retry, rate-limit and failure behavior.

rules.title: Validate and sanitize external data
rules.detail: Treat third-party payloads as untrusted; validate schema, size, identifiers and content before persistence or business use.
rules.example_good: The implementation and review evidence demonstrate: Validate and sanitize external data.
rules.example_bad: The change violates or ignores the rule: Validate and sanitize external data.

rules.title: Map external identifiers and status values explicitly
rules.detail: Do not leak unstable vendor enums or IDs throughout the domain; maintain a documented mapping and unknown-value handling.
rules.example_good: The implementation and review evidence demonstrate: Map external identifiers and status values explicitly.
rules.example_bad: The change violates or ignores the rule: Map external identifiers and status values explicitly.

rules.title: Protect credentials and callback endpoints
rules.detail: Use scoped credentials, rotation, signature verification where available and safe secret storage.
rules.example_good: The implementation and review evidence demonstrate: Protect credentials and callback endpoints.
rules.example_bad: The change violates or ignores the rule: Protect credentials and callback endpoints.

rules.title: Provide observability and reconciliation
rules.detail: Log/measure correlation IDs, attempts, latency and failures and provide a reconciliation path for business-critical integrations.
rules.example_good: The implementation and review evidence demonstrate: Provide observability and reconciliation.
rules.example_bad: The change violates or ignores the rule: Provide observability and reconciliation.

integration_guide.title: Resolve applicability and dependencies
integration_guide.description: Confirm where STD-INTEGRATION applies and resolve its extends/implements/uses/aligns_with dependencies in the project standard profile.

integration_guide.title: Record project decisions
integration_guide.description: Apply the rules of Third-Party Integration to requirements/design/ADRs and record any project-specific thresholds, providers or justified exceptions.

integration_guide.title: Implement with evidence
integration_guide.description: Implement the applicable MUST/SHOULD rules and link code, configuration, tests or review evidence to the change.

integration_guide.title: Verify before completion
integration_guide.description: Run automated checks where possible and manual review for judgement-based rules; close or approve documented deviations.

common_issues.issue: Third-Party Integration is applied inconsistently across features
common_issues.cause: The project references the standard but does not resolve concrete ownership, thresholds or verification evidence.
common_issues.solution: Resolve dependencies, record project-specific decisions and include applicable rules in implementation/review checks.

common_issues.issue: Implementation satisfies the happy path but misses Third-Party Integration failure cases
common_issues.cause: Boundary, retry, security or recovery scenarios were not included in acceptance/test planning.
common_issues.solution: Use the standard rules to add explicit failure/recovery scenarios and verify them before release.
